# MSX-MUSIC BASIC Extension V2 New Features

> This is an English translation of the [Japanese original](../new-feature.md). Where the two differ, the Japanese version is authoritative.

This document covers only **the differences between MSX-MUSIC BASIC Extension V2 and the original MSX-MUSIC BASIC extension**.
For the full specification of the statements and MML, see [`basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md).

**Its readers include people who write applications for MSX.** It also touches on ROM addresses and the MSX work area. If you only want to play music from BASIC, [`basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md) alone is enough.

There are four kinds of differences.

| | |
|---|---|
| [Added statements](#added-statements) | Features that did not exist previously |
| [Extended statements](#extended-statements) | Existed previously, but now accept more values |
| [Added MML commands](#added-mml-commands) | Forms that were previously an error, or were previously ignored |
| [Commands whose behavior changed](#commands-whose-behavior-changed) | Could be written previously, but the meaning has changed |

In addition, [One ROM for all machines](#one-rom-for-all-machines) describes the differences that come from combining the builds for MSX2+ and earlier and for turbo R into one.

## Added statements

### CALL MUSIC(-1) — releasing the BASIC extension

```
CALL MUSIC(-1)
```

Returns everything that `CALL MUSIC` initialized, and goes back to the state before initialization.

- Stops playback and keys off all channels
- Restores the interrupt hook (`H.TIMI`) and fills the PLAY statement hook (`H.PLAY`) with RET (if something was using `H.PLAY` before `CALL MUSIC`, that is not restored)
- Returns 965 bytes (1255 bytes on the MSX Sound Suite cartridge build) to `HIMEM`
- It goes back to the uninitialized state, so **`CALL MUSIC` can initialize again**

```basic
10 CALL MUSIC(0, 0, 1, 1, 1)
20 PLAY#2, "O4CDE", "O4EGB", "O3C1"
30 CALL MUSIC(-1)             ' return the work area and the interrupt
40 PRINT FRE(0)
```

Because the interrupt hook is removed, a program that has finished using the BASIC extension can get rid of the overhead of interrupt handling.

Like `CALL MUSIC`, it internally does the equivalent of `CLEAR`, so **all BASIC variables are cleared after it runs.**

It gives `Illegal function call` in the following cases.

| | |
|---|---|
| Not initialized | Called without `CALL MUSIC` having been executed |
| Something hooked the interrupt afterwards | `H.TIMI` does not point to the BASIC extension |

The latter is refused because it would drop that hook out of the interrupt chain, and there would be no way to restore it.

### CALL AUDIO / CALL MINIT / CALL OPM / CALL MIDI — handing over page 1

**Added only in the ROM for the Y8960 cartridge.** The ROM used as a replacement for the built-in MSX-MUSIC does not take these names.

```
CALL AUDIO      ' to MSX-AUDIO BASIC Extension Lite
CALL MINIT      ' to Y8960 BASIC Extension
CALL OPM        ' to OPM BASIC Extension
CALL MIDI       ' to MIDI Play BASIC Extension
```

Hands page 1 over to another sound chip BASIC extension carried on the same cartridge. **The arguments are read by the destination**, so the `(2)` of `CALL MINIT(2)` is not interpreted by MSX-MUSIC BASIC Extension V2.

Before handing over, it performs by itself the same cleanup as `CALL MUSIC(-1)` (stopping playback, returning the hooks and work area), so the user is not required to finish explicitly. It can hand over even when `CALL MUSIC` has not been executed. This ROM itself is what `CALL MUSIC` switches back in.

For the same reason as `CALL MUSIC(-1)`, if something hooked `H.TIMI` after this BASIC extension, the result is `Illegal function call`.

**In the ROM for the Y8960 cartridge, FM-BIOS and this BASIC extension cannot be used at the same time.** The body of FM-BIOS is in another bank, and calling FM-BIOS returns with the second half of page 1 still switched to that bank. Therefore the machine crashes: at the next interrupt if FM-BIOS is called while still initialized with `CALL MUSIC`, and at that interrupt if a `CALL` statement of this BASIC extension is executed while FM-BIOS is being called from an interrupt. Release it with `CALL MUSIC(-1)` before using FM-BIOS. The ROM used as a replacement for the built-in MSX-MUSIC does not have this restriction.

### CALL MIXER — the cartridge's mixer

**Added only in the ROM for the Y8960 cartridge.**

```
CALL MIXER(<master>, <SSGS>, <OPLLEX>, <OPL2EX>, <SCC>, <OPM>)
```

Sets the six volumes of the cartridge's hardware mixer. Each is 0-128: 0 is silent and 128 is maximum. None of the six can be omitted. If even one is out of range, the result is `Illegal function call` and the mixer does not change. It can be used even when `CALL MUSIC` has not been executed, and `CALL MUSIC` and `CALL MUSIC(-1)` do not touch the mixer.

**This ROM sets all six to 128 at startup and when switched in from another BASIC extension.** Startup includes a restart without a reset, so an application that uses FM-BIOS as it is does not inherit the mixer values left by a previously running program.

The mixer applies only to the sound chips inside the cartridge; the volume of the internal PSG and the internal OPLL does not change. For details, see [`basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md#call-mixermaster-ssgs-opllex-opl2ex-scc-opm).

### CALL VOICE MODE — playing library voices without substituting built-in voices

```
CALL VOICE MODE(<mode>)
```

The 15 voices of the voice library (those marked `*` in the voice library list of the reference) are played by substituting OPLL built-in voices, as before. The library also holds voice parameters for them, but they sound different from the built-in voices, and previously they could be neither played nor taken out with `CALL VOICE COPY`.

| `<mode>` | `@0`-`@63` |
|--:|---|
| 0 | Same as before. The 15 voices in the table below select OPLL built-in voices |
| 1 | No substitution. Every number loads the library's voice parameters into the user voice (built-in voice number 0) |

The numbers substituted in mode 0, and the OPLL built-in voice numbers they select (the upper 4 bits of registers `30H`-`38H`):

| `@n` | 0 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 9 | 10 | 12 | 14 | 16 | 23 | 24 | 33 | 48 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Built-in voice | 3 | 1 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 2 | 15 | 11 | 12 | 13 | 10 | 14 | 9 |

```basic
10 CALL MUSIC
20 CALL VOICE MODE(1)
30 DIM V%(16) : CALL VOICE COPY(@2, V%)   ' Illegal function call in mode 0
40 PLAY#2, "@2O4C"                        ' plays with the library's Violin voice parameters
```

- The mode applies to MML `@0`-`@63`, to numbers written with `@` in `CALL VOICE`, and to source numbers of `CALL VOICE COPY`. It has nothing to do with the OPLLEX ROM voice banks (`@64` and above)
- MML `@n` is queued and read in the mode in effect when it is played. Changing the mode during playback makes the new mode apply from the `@n` that have not been played yet
- In mode 1, every voice uses the user voice. There is only one user voice, so only one voice can sound at a time
- Initialization (the first `CALL MUSIC`, or a `CALL MUSIC` after `CALL MUSIC(-1)`) sets mode 0. Executing `CALL MUSIC` again while already initialized does not change the mode
- A `<mode>` other than 0 and 1 gives `Illegal function call`

## Extended statements

### CALL AUDREG — OPLLEX bank registers and panning

```
CALL AUDREG(<register number>, <value>)
```

The accepted register numbers now include the OPLLEX bank registers **`40H`-`48H`** and panning **`50H`-`58H`**. Both are in the order of channels 1-9. The ranges accepted previously (`00H`-`07H`, `0EH`-`18H`, `20H`-`28H`, `30H`-`38H`) are unchanged.

```basic
CALL AUDREG(&H40, 3)   ' set the ROM voice bank of channel 1 to 3 (VRC7)
CALL AUDREG(&H50, 1)   ' channel 1 to the far left
```

### CALL VOICE COPY — waveform selection DM / DC

**bit0 of offsets 21 and 29** of the voice parameters is assigned to the waveform selection (DM / DC) of the modulator and of the carrier respectively.

| Value | Waveform |
|---|---|
| 0 | Sine wave |
| 1 | Half-wave rectified |

```basic
10 DIM V%(16)
20 CALL VOICE COPY(@35, V%)     ' take Brass out into the array
30 V%(14) = V%(14) OR &H0100    ' set bit0 of offset 29 = DC
40 CALL VOICE COPY(V%, @63)     ' write it back to number 63
50 CALL VOICE(@63)
```

> Each array element is 2 bytes, so offset 21 is the high byte of `V%(10)` and offset 29 is the high byte of `V%(14)`.

Previously these 2 bytes were a reserved area, and the original code did not read them. All the voice library presets have 0 there, so **how library voices sound does not change.**

However, previously, loading a voice left DM / DC of register `03H` as they were. Now they are rewritten with the values in the voice parameters, so if you set DM / DC with `Y3,` or `CALL AUDREG(3, …)` and then select a voice, the waveform returns to the value in the voice parameters (a sine wave for library voices).

### PLAY #1 / #3 — the six SSGS channels

**An extension of the MSX Sound Suite cartridge build only.** The Y8960's SSGS has two sets of sound generators of the same form as the PSG, and the first set is at the same register numbers as the internal PSG. The original three PSG channels play the first set, and the cartridge build adds three channels that play the second set (`10H`-`1DH`). The internal PSG receives the same writes as the first set, so it sounds along with it.

| Mode | Previously | Cartridge build |
|---|---|---|
| `#1` | `Illegal function call` | PSG 3 + second set 3 |
| `#3` | Same as `#2` | `#2` + second set 3 |

```basic
PLAY#1, "O4C", "O4E", "O4G", "O5C", "O5E", "O5G"   ' six parts
```

- The strings are the three for PSG followed by the three for the second set. The string numbers of `CALL PLAY` are in the same order
- `PLAY` with `#0`, `#2`, or without `#` is as before, and the second set does not sound
- `Yr, d` can write `00H`-`0DH` and `10H`-`1DH` on all six channels. The number decides which set it reaches; the channel does not change that. The second set cannot be read back, so the mask uses the record of the values written
- The SSGS's own channel volume (`20H`-`22H`, `24H`-`26H`) and panning (`28H`-`2AH`, `2CH`-`2EH`) can also be written with `Y`. `CALL MUSIC`, and stopping playback (`CALL STOPM`, CTRL-STOP, an error in this BASIC extension), set the volume to maximum (128) and the panning to center (128)
- The channel volume can also be written with `@V` on PSG channels ([@Vn — SSGS channel volume on PSG](#vn--ssgs-channel-volume-on-psg))
- The replacement build also accepts the register numbers of the second set and of the SSGS itself, but writes nothing. MML written for the cartridge build runs as it is
- The memory that `CALL MUSIC` allocates below HIMEM is 1255 bytes (965 on the replacement build)

The replacement build for the built-in MSX-MUSIC does not have this. For details, see "The six SSGS channels" in [`basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md).

## Added MML commands

### Length 0 and R0 — sounding and silencing without consuming time

| Form | Action |
|---|---|
| `C0` `D0` … `B0` | Issues **only a note-on**. Consumes no time |
| `R0` | Issues **only a note-off**. Consumes no time |
| `@Wn` | Waits for the length of an nth note while still sounding |

Combining these three, **you can move the pitch, volume and voice within a single note**.

```basic
PLAY#2, "T120O4C0@W8P100@W8P200@W8R0"
```

`C0` issues a note-on, then the pitch is raised to 100 and then 200 cents while waiting an eighth note each time, and finally `R0` issues a note-off. The total length is three eighth notes.

**Restriction — a second note cannot be placed without advancing time.** After a note of length 0, unless something that advances time (`@Wn`, or an `Rn` with a length) is placed before the next note, the result is `Illegal function call`. This is because keying on twice in the same tick only overwrites the first one, which is meaningless.

```basic
PLAY#2, "C0D0"      ' → Illegal function call
PLAY#2, "C0R0D0"    ' → Illegal function call (R0 does not advance time)
PLAY#2, "C0@W8D0"   ' → OK
PLAY#2, "C0R4D0"    ' → OK
```

`L0` and `@W0` give `Illegal function call`. Write length 0 explicitly on each note, as in `C0`.

Usable on both FM and PSG.

> A length of 0 on a note name could also be written previously, and it took the same `Ln` length as when the length is omitted. **The meaning of `C0` has changed** ([Commands whose behavior changed](#commands-whose-behavior-changed)). `R0` was previously `Illegal function call`.

### Pitch bend P / @P

| Form | Meaning | Range |
|---|---|---|
| `Pn` | Pitch bend in cents (absolute value) | -1200 to 1200 |
| `@Pn` | Added to the current bend value | -1200 to 1200 |

100 cents is a semitone, and 1200 cents is one octave. The range of `@Pn` applies to the **difference**, so by accumulating them the total can exceed 1200 cents.

It is an additive term independent of transpose (`CALL TRANSPOSE`) and pitch (`CALL PITCH`), so their settings are kept. **It takes effect immediately even on a sounding note**, so use it together with `@W`.

```basic
PLAY#2, "O4C0@W4@P50@W4@P50@W4@P50@W4R0"   ' raise by 50 cents at a time
PLAY#2, "P-50O4CDEFG"                      ' play everything 50 cents lower
```

Usable on both FM and PSG.

### Portamento ~

Placing `~` before a note makes the pitch **move smoothly** to that note.

```basic
PLAY#2, "O4C4~E4"        ' rises from C to E over a quarter note
PLAY#2, "O4~-1200C4"     ' scoops up to C from one octave below
```

**The speed is not specified.** The time the move takes is the length of the target note, and the pitch arrives exactly when that note ends. To move fast, combine it with `&` and extend the sound after the slide.

```basic
PLAY#2, "O4~-400C16&C4"  ' scoop up over a sixteenth note, then hold for a quarter note
```

There are four ways to specify the start point.

| Form | Start point | Sounding |
|---|---|---|
| `A~B` | The pitch now sounding | Not re-sounded |
| `C0~B` | Given explicitly by the length-0 note `C0`. The same mechanism as above | `C0` sounds it |
| `~<cent>B` | The pitch `<cent>` away from `B` (-1200 to 1200) | Re-sounded |
| `~B` (no note immediately before; the same after a rest and at the start of a PLAY statement) | Treated as `~0`. That is, it sounds normally | Re-sounded |

As in `C0~E4`, **the start point can be written as a note name by using a note of length 0**, so there is no need to count cent values.

When chained, each one heads again toward the next note. If the next note comes before the pitch arrives, **the pitch sounding at that moment** becomes the next start point.

```basic
PLAY#2, "O4C4~E4~G4"
```

It coexists with a static pitch bend given by `P` / `@P`. Portamento converges toward that setting, and the bend remains after it ends.

**Restrictions.** Between `~` and the target note, only `O` `<` `>` `L` `T` `Q` `{` and spaces can be placed. On PSG channels, `V` `S` `M` can also be placed. `V` and `S` take effect together with the target note, and writing `S` restarts the envelope there. `M` does not apply to a note that slides; it takes effect from the next note. A target in another octave can be written as `C4~>C4`. Place `V` on FM channels, commands that act on the sound chip such as `Y` and `P`, rests, `@W`, and `&` **before** `~`. Placing them in between gives `Illegal function call`. The same applies when the string ends with `~`. **The target note must not have length 0.** It is not an error, but how it sounds is not defined.

```basic
PLAY#2, "O4C4~>C4"     ' OK. To the C one octave up
PLAY#2, "O4C4V10~E4"   ' OK
PLAY#2, "O4C4~V10E4"   ' → Illegal function call
```

Usable on both FM and PSG, and **both move along a logarithmic curve that advances by an equal number of cents every tick**. The same MML gives the same curve whether it is put on FM or on PSG.

### Dotted rest R.

A dot can also be put on a rest, as in `R.`. It can be combined with a length, as in `R8.`.

```basic
PLAY#2, "O4C8.R8.C8.R8."
```

> **`R` does not look at the value of `L`.** An `R` with its length omitted is a quarter rest (equivalent to `R4`) regardless of the `L` setting. This is the original behavior. Inside `{ }` it takes the tuplet length ([R — takes the tuplet length inside a tuplet](#r--takes-the-tuplet-length-inside-a-tuplet)). To match `Ln`, write `Rn` explicitly.

### OPLLEX ROM voice banks

The Y8960's extended OPLL part (OPLLEX) has four banks of ROM preset voices, selectable per channel. Specifying 64 or above for MML `@n` plays a voice from that bank.

| n | Bank | Voice number |
|---|---|---|
| 65-79 | 0 (OPLL) | 1-15 |
| 81-95 | 1 (OPLL-X) | 1-15 |
| 97-111 | 2 (OPLL-P) | 1-15 |
| 113-127 | 3 (VRC7) | 1-15 |

In the value n minus 64, bit5-4 is the bank and bit3-0 is the voice number.

```basic
PLAY#2, "@113O4CDE"   ' play with voice 1 of VRC7
```

Voice number 0 is the user voice and the banks do not have it, so `@64` `@80` `@96` `@112` select the [user voice](#user-voices-64--80--96--112) instead of a bank voice. 128 and above give `Illegal function call`.

**It cannot be specified in `CALL VOICE`.** `CALL VOICE(@113)` gives `Illegal function call`. Specify bank voices with MML `@n`.

### User voices 64 / 80 / 96 / 112

**Present in both the replacement build for the built-in MSX-MUSIC and the MSX Sound Suite cartridge build.** They can be used without OPLLEX. The numbers use the gaps in the OPLLEX ROM voice banks (voice number 0 of each bank).

Previously there was only one user voice, `@63`. Four are added, `@64` `@80` `@96` `@112`, so five sets of voice parameters can now be held.

| | Previously | Extended |
|---|---|---|
| MML `@n` | `@64` and above are errors | `@64` `@80` `@96` `@112` select user voices |
| `CALL VOICE` | 0-63 | 0-63, 64, 80, 96, 112 |
| Destination of `CALL VOICE COPY` | 63 only | 63, 64, 80, 96, 112 |
| Source of `CALL VOICE COPY` | 0-63 (except those marked `*`) | 64, 80, 96, 112 in addition |

```basic
10 CALL MUSIC
20 CALL VOICE COPY(@35, @64)         ' Brass to number 64
30 CALL VOICE COPY(@45, @80)         ' Synthesizer Violin to number 80
40 PLAY#2, "@64O4CDE@80O4CDE"
```

**Only one user voice can sound at a time, as before.** The OPLL has only one set of user voice registers (`00H`-`07H`), and the OPLLEX banks do not apply to the user voice either. Each time one is selected with `@n`, the voice parameters of that number are loaded into the user voice registers.

- The voice parameters are placed in the block that `CALL MUSIC` allocates below HIMEM. Its contents become 0 when it is allocated, and they remain when `CALL MUSIC` is executed again while already initialized. The allocation is 128 bytes larger for this
- Usable whether or not OPLLEX is present. Selecting one also writes the bank register, but a plain OPLL does not take in that address

**FM channels only.** `@n` on PSG channels has a different meaning ([@n — PSG tone/noise and envelope](#n--psg-tonenoise-and-envelope)).

`@0`-`@63` always play in bank 0, so **how the original voice numbers sound does not change.**

**Whether OPLLEX is present is not checked.** On a plain OPLL, which has no bank registers, the write is simply ignored; it is not an error, and the bank 0 voice plays.

### Third argument of Y — masked writes

```
Yr, d, m     m = 0-255 (0 when omitted)
```

**Writing a third argument to `Y` lets you rewrite only part of a register.** Previously this was `Illegal function call`.

```
r <- (current value of r AND m) OR d
```

Bits where m is 1 keep the current value, and bits where it is 0 take the value of d. When one register packs several parameters, you can touch only the bits you want without knowing the current values of the other parameters.

```basic
PLAY#2, "", "", "", "", "Y7,1,254"   ' set only bit0 of register 7 to 1
```

PSG register 7 is the mixer: bit2-0 enable tone and bit5-3 enable noise, one bit per channel (0 enables). The example above has m=254, that is, it keeps everything except bit0 as it is and rewrites only the tone of A to disabled.

`Yr, d` with m omitted is the same as m=0, and **the whole register becomes d. The meaning of the previous way of writing does not change.**

It can be written the same way on FM channels. The OPLL cannot read back its registers, so the record of the values written is used; the record covers every register that `Y` accepts, so **m also works on the OPLLEX bank registers `40H`-`48H` and panning `50H`-`58H`.**

### Hexadecimal literals `$`

```
$nn        Always 2 digits. $00-$FF
```

**Putting `$` before a number lets you write it in hexadecimal.** Previously only decimal could be written.

```basic
PLAY#2, "Y$30,$53"                       ' 53H to register 30H
PLAY#2, "", "", "", "", "Y$06,$0A,$10"   ' 0AH to register 6, keeping bit4
PLAY#2, "@$0A O$04 C$10"                 ' anywhere a number can be written
```

`A`-`F` may be upper or lower case. For a negative value, write `-` first.

```basic
PLAY#2, "P-$64"     ' -100 cents
```

**The number of digits is fixed at two.** `A`-`F` are both hexadecimal digits and note names, so if digits were read until they ran out, a note name placed after the number would also be taken into it. Because counting ends at two digits, nothing written after it is added to the number.

```basic
PLAY#2, "Y$20,$0FCDE"    ' 0FH to register 20H, then the notes C D E
PLAY#2, "Y$30,$1AC4"     ' 1AH to register 30H, then C as a quarter note
```

**Ending with one digit gives `Illegal function call`.** If `$F` were allowed, it could not be told apart from `$FC` when a `C` follows, so write it with two digits as `$0F`. Write `O$4` as `O$04`, and `C$0` as `C$00`.

**Values whose absolute value is 256 or more cannot be written in hexadecimal.** Write `Mn` (1-65535), and values of `Pn` `@Pn` `~n` (±1200) whose absolute value is 256 or more, in decimal.

**Only a length of 0 is written in decimal.** `C$00` and `R$00` do not become a note or rest that consumes no time; they are treated the same as when the length is omitted (`C$00` has the length of `Ln`, and `R$00` is the same as `R` with the length omitted).

Nothing changes in how decimal is written.

### Panpot `I`

```
In        n = 0-255
```

The OPLLEX (extended OPLL) and the SSGS (the PSG-compatible sound part) of the Y8960 cartridge have **a panpot for each channel**. `I` sets that panning. The value is written to the chip's register as is.

| n | Panning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Far left |
| 128 | Center |
| 255 | Far right |
| 0 | Undefined. It can be written, but how it sounds is not guaranteed |

In between is power panning; at the center, both left and right are −3 dB.

```basic
PLAY#2, "I1O4CDE", "I255O4GAB"                   ' 1st FM string to the left, 2nd to the right
PLAY#2, "", "", "", "", "I1O4CDE", "I255O4GAB"   ' PSG 1ch to the left, 2ch to the right
```

- On FM channels, the panning of all FM sound chip channels assigned to that string changes. It is written to OPLLEX `50H`-`58H` (channels 1-9)
- In the rhythm sound string, the panning of channels 7, 8 and 9 changes together. The rhythm sounds play at the panning of these three channels (the bass drum on 7, the hi-hat and snare on 8, the tom and cymbal on 9). To set instruments separately, write them with `Y$56`-`Y$58`
- On PSG channels, the panning of that channel itself changes. It is written to SSGS `28H`-`2AH`, and for the second set of the cartridge build, `2CH`-`2EH`
- `CALL MUSIC` sets all channels to the center (128). The panning of PSG channels also returns to the center when playback stops (`CALL STOPM`, CTRL-STOP, an error of this BASIC extension)
- It consumes no time, and any number of them can be lined up

**On a machine without the Y8960 cartridge, nothing happens.** The OPLLEX panning is outside the OPLL's address range, and a plain OPLL does not take in the address itself. The SSGS responds to the same I/O ports as the internal PSG, and selects itself with register numbers that the internal PSG does not interpret. In both cases, without the extension parts the writes reach nowhere and vanish. It is not an error either, so it can be written regardless of the machine.

Note that the correspondence between values and panning is based on the cartridge specification (2026-10-17 edition), and it has not been confirmed by playing on actual OPLLEX and SSGS hardware.

### Tuplets `{ }n` — PSG channels

```
{ notes... }n        n = 1-64; Ln when omitted
```

`{ }n` already existed on FM channels in the original, but on PSG channels it was `Illegal function call`. **It can now be written on the three PSG channels as well.**

```basic
PLAY#2, "", "", "", "", "T120L4{CDE}4"   ' three 12th notes = one quarter note
```

The specification is the same as on FM: `R` with the length omitted takes the tuplet length, and `@Wn` does not take the tuplet length. See "Tuplets `{ }n`" in [`basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md).

**The PSG tuplet lengths are placed in the block that `CALL MUSIC` allocates below HIMEM.** FM can hold one byte in the VCB of each channel, but the PSG VCBs are in the MSX system area from `0FB41H` onward with no room to spare, and the corresponding byte there is filled with the tick count of that item for each note. That block also holds the FM voice parameters, the PSG portamento state, the temperament table, and user voices 64, 80, 96 and 112, and the memory that `CALL MUSIC` allocates is 965 bytes, 158 bytes more than the previous 807 bytes (portamento state 15, tuplet lengths 3, temperament table 12, user voices 128). The cartridge build further adds the three channels of the SSGS second set, the record of the SSGS's own channel volume and panning, and user voice 63, for 1255 bytes (in the replacement build, user voice 63 is in the MSX work area).

---

## Commands whose behavior changed

The following keep the same way of writing but change meaning.

| | Applies to | Previously | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Length 0 on a note name (`C0` and so on) | FM, PSG | The length of `Ln`, the same as with the length omitted | Outputs only the note-on and consumes no time ([Length 0 and R0](#length-0-and-r0--sounding-and-silencing-without-consuming-time)) |
| `R` with the length omitted inside `{ }` | FM, PSG | Quarter rest | Tuplet length |
| `@Wn` | PSG | Same as `Rn` (silences, then waits) | Waits while still sounding |
| `@n` | PSG | Accepts 0-63 and ignores it | Switches tone/noise and envelope. Accepts n of 0-127 |
| `@Vn` | PSG | Accepts 0-127 and ignores it | The cartridge build writes the SSGS channel volume. Accepts n of 0-128 |
| `Yr, d` | PSG | Only reads and discards the arguments; does nothing | Writes to PSG registers. The accepted r changes from 0-200 to 0-13 and the SSGS numbers |
| `&` | PSG | Is ignored | Works as tie/legato |

The handling of tempo fractions has also changed, on both FM and PSG ([PLAY tempo accuracy](#play-tempo-accuracy)).

### @Wn — PSG also keeps sounding

```
@Wn      n = 1-64 (the length of Ln when omitted)
```

`@W` is a command that FM channels have had since the original; it waits for the length of an nth note without a note-off. **On PSG channels it was the same as `Rn` and the sound stopped, but it now keeps the sound, the same as on FM.** An envelope set with `S` also continues without restarting. When `V` or `S` is rewritten between the note and `@Wn`, that `@Wn` restarts it.

```basic
PLAY#2, "", "", "", "", "O4C0@W8P100@W8P200@W8R0"   ' raise the pitch while still sounding
```

`@W0` is `Illegal function call` (an `@W` that does not wait has no meaning).

### @n — PSG tone/noise and envelope

```
@n       n = 0-127
```

Previously, `@n` on PSG channels accepted 0-63 and did nothing. **It now specifies, in one byte, the tone/noise output switching of the channel and the hardware envelope selection.**

| Bit | Contents |
|---|---|
| bit4-0 | When bit4 is 1, hardware envelope (bit4 of the amplitude register). Then bit3-0 are the envelope shape (R13) |
| bit5 | Tone. **Sounds at 0** |
| bit6 | Noise. **Sounds at 1** (the opposite of bit5) |

```basic
PLAY#2, "", "", "", "", "Y6,5@96O4C4"   ' play with noise only
PLAY#2, "", "", "", "", "@88M2000O4C2"   ' tone + noise, envelope shape 8
```

`@0` is the normal state, tone only. `@16`+*s* selects the same envelope as `S`*s*, and at the same time sets that channel to tone only. It rewrites only that channel's two bits of register 7, and the settings of the other channels and of the joystick ports remain. It consumes no time. For the full specification, see "`@n` on PSG channels" in [`basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md).

**If MML written for the original puts `@n` on PSG channels, how it sounds may change.** An `@n` with bit4 at 0 (`@0`-`@15`, `@32`-`@47`) turns off the envelope, so it has an effect when written after `S`. `@0`-`@31` set that channel to tone only, so they have an effect when written after the mixer has been changed with `Y7`. An `@n` with bit4 at 1 (`@16`-`@31`, `@48`-`@63`) applies the envelope, and `@32`-`@63` stop the tone.

### @Vn — SSGS channel volume on PSG

```
@Vn      n = 0-128
```

Previously, `@V` on PSG channels accepted 0-127 and did nothing. **In the cartridge build, it now writes the volume of that SSGS channel (`20H`-`22H`, `24H`-`26H`).** 0 is silent, 128 is maximum, and in between is proportional to the value.

```basic
PLAY#1, "@V64O4C", "", "", "@V128O4E"   ' first set A at half, second set A at maximum
```

- It is a volume separate from `V`, and the actual volume is the two multiplied. `V` is a 4-bit volume as before
- It affects only the SSGS output. The volume of the internal PSG, which sounds together with the first set, does not change
- It returns to 128 at `CALL MUSIC` and when playback stops (`CALL STOPM`, CTRL-STOP, an error of this BASIC extension). It consumes no time
- The replacement build accepts 0-128 and does nothing

**If MML written for the original puts `@V` on PSG channels, the SSGS volume changes in the cartridge build.** If the same string as for FM is also passed to PSG, the fine volume values meant for FM become the SSGS channel volume as they are.

### Yr, d — writing PSG registers

```
Yr, d
```

**`Y` on PSG channels writes d to PSG register r (0-13).** Previously it only read and discarded the arguments and did nothing, and the accepted range of r was 0-200. It also accepts the register numbers of the SSGS second set and of the SSGS itself (`10H`-`1DH`, part of `20H`-`2EH`); the cartridge build writes there, and the replacement build writes nothing ([PLAY #1 / #3](#play-1--3--the-six-ssgs-channels)).

```basic
PLAY#2, "", "", "", "", "Y6,17R4"   ' 17 to PSG register 6 (noise period)
```

`Y` on FM channels writes to OPLL registers as before. The OPLLEX bank registers `40H`-`48H` and panning `50H`-`58H` have been added to the accepted r.

On either kind of channel it consumes no time, and any number of them can be lined up.

```basic
PLAY#2, "", "", "", "", "Y6,23Y2,7Y3,1R4"   ' three in a row, and the length is still R4
```

For the third argument that rewrites only part of a register, see [Third argument of Y](#third-argument-of-y--masked-writes).

### & — legato on PSG

`&` was previously ignored on PSG channels, but **it now works as tie/legato, the same as on FM.**

- If the notes before and after are the **same**, it joins the lengths without sounding again (tie)
- If the notes before and after are **different**, it replaces only the pitch without restarting the envelope
  (legato)

```basic
PLAY#2, "", "", "", "", "S1M2000O4C4&D4&E4"
```

PSG has no key-on, so what `&` suppresses is the restart of the envelope. It has an effect when the envelope is used with `S`.

`&` on FM channels is as before: when the notes before and after differ, it replaces only the pitch without outputting key-off/key-on.

### R — takes the tuplet length inside a tuplet

Previously, `R` inside `{ }` was a quarter rest when its length was omitted. **It now takes the tuplet length.**

```basic
PLAY#2, "T120L4{CDR}4"   ' two 12th notes and a 12th rest = one quarter note
```

`R` is counted among the notes as before; only its length now matches. `R.` takes the tuplet length with a dot.

**`R` outside a tuplet does not change.** With the length omitted it is still a quarter rest. `{CDR12}4`, with the length written, does not change either.

### PLAY tempo accuracy

The calculation of note length fractions has changed from quantization in steps of 1/32 to exact retention in units of 1/tempo, and **the tempo error of performances that contain many dotted notes is smaller.**

The measured values, comparing the average over 64 notes with the ideal value, are as follows.

| | Previously | Now |
|---|--:|--:|
| `T110 L4` | +0.069% | -0.026% |
| `T110 L4.` | +0.833% | -0.026% |
| `T63 L3` | +0.037% | -0.004% |

For combinations that divide evenly, such as `T120 L4`, the error is 0 both previously and now.

In addition, a problem where the fractions of some channels were carried over across PLAY statements has been fixed.

### How PLAY receives its strings

**However many strings made with `+` or functions are lined up in one `PLAY` statement, each one plays as written.** Previously, an earlier string could be overwritten by a later string.

```basic
T$="E4"
PLAY#2, "C4"+T$, "D4"+T$    ' 1st plays C E, 2nd plays D E
```

Even when the string area runs short and is reorganized, strings written earlier (including variables) are not corrupted.

**Built strings are limited to 10 per `PLAY` statement**, and the 11th gives `String formula too complex`. String constants and variables are not counted.

Also, a problem has been fixed where, after a `PLAY` that ran into an error (such as `1/0`) while evaluating its strings, a `PLAY` with fewer strings could fail to return.

---

## One ROM for all machines

The differences between the version for MSX2+ and earlier and the version for turbo R have **all been replaced with run-time branches**, and for both the BASIC extension and GBIOS, **a single binary runs on both kinds of machine**.

As a result, the three statements that existed only in the turbo R version are accepted as syntax on every machine.

| Statement | turbo R | Others |
|---|---|---|
| `CALL PCM PLAY` | Works | `Illegal function call` |
| `CALL PCM REC` | Works | `Illegal function call` |
| `CALL PAUSE` | Works | `Illegal function call` |

These three depend on the PCM entries and the system timer of the turbo R MAIN-ROM, so there is nothing that run-time branching can absorb.

---

## Differences between sound chips

Of the added features, the following use the extension parts that the Y8960 cartridge carries — OPLLEX (extended OPLL) and SSGS (PSG-compatible part). **Neither extension part is checked for presence**, so on a machine that lacks them, the writes simply reach nowhere and vanish, and there is no error. The same program runs on either machine.

| Feature | Extension part used | Behavior on a machine without the extension part |
|---|---|---|
| `@65`-`@127` (ROM voice banks) | OPLLEX (extended OPLL) | The voice with the same number in bank 0 plays |
| `Y$40`-`Y$48`, `CALL AUDREG(&H40)`-`(&H48)` | OPLLEX | Accepted, but the sound does not change |
| `In` on FM channels, `Y$50`-`Y$58`, `CALL AUDREG(&H50)`-`(&H58)` | OPLLEX | Accepted, but the panning does not change |
| `In` on PSG channels (panpot) | SSGS (PSG-compatible part) | Accepted, but the panning does not change |

A plain OPLL takes in an address only when its upper two bits are 00, so writes to the bank registers and panning do not wrap around (`40H` to `00H`, `50H` to `10H`) and corrupt user voices or pitches. The SSGS panpot uses register numbers that the internal PSG does not interpret, so those writes are likewise discarded there.

**The record of values written to OPLL registers is kept whether or not OPLLEX is present.** The bank registers and panning are also in the record, so a masked write such as `Y$40, $03, $FC` produces the same value on either machine.

This does not depend on which ROM is used (the replacement build for the built-in MSX-MUSIC, or the MSX Sound Suite cartridge build). Only the sound chips present decide it. The exceptions are [the six SSGS channels](#play-1--3--the-six-ssgs-channels), writes with `Y` to the SSGS second set and to the SSGS's own channel volume and panning, and `@V` on PSG channels, which take effect only in the cartridge build (the replacement build accepts them and does nothing).

---

## Combining them

Notes of length 0, `@W`, `P` / `@P` and `~` were provided together **to build a time axis within a single note**.

```basic
10 CALL MUSIC(0, 0, 1, 1, 1)
20 ' vibrato
30 PLAY#2, "T120@35O4C0@W16@P30@W16@P-60@W16@P60@W16@P-30@W16R0"
40 ' scoop up into the note
50 PLAY#2, "T120@35O4~-500C8&C2"
60 ' portamento over three notes
70 PLAY#2, "T120@45O4C4~E4~G4>~C2"
```

PSG can be written the same way. This example does not use rhythm and assigns three channels to FM, so PSG takes the 4th to 6th strings.

```basic
80 PLAY#2, "", "", "", "T120S1M3000O4~-700C4~E4~G2"
```

---

## What has not changed

For backward compatibility, the following are kept as they were in the original.

| | |
|---|---|
| Addresses referenced from outside | The ROM header (in the MSX Sound Suite cartridge build, MSX Sound Suite uses the reserved `400AH`-`400BH` and `4010H`-`4017H`), the `APRLOPLL` signature at `4018H`, the version string at `4100H`, the MBIOS entry table at `4110H`, and the BASIC extension entries at `5000H`, `5003H` and `5006H` |
| GBIOS automatic playback | `MSTART` / `MSTOP` / `OPLDRV` / `TSTBGM` / `RDDATA` |
| Voice library | The 64 voices `@0`-`@63` are unmodified |
| The 27 statements from MSX-AUDIO | Accepted as syntax as before, and return `Illegal function call` |
| MML for FM channels | Of what could be written previously, only length 0 on note names and `R` with the length omitted inside tuplets have changed meaning (in addition, the handling of tempo fractions has changed) |
